title: Improving Performance with Fast Alphas
summary: Fixed-parent execution screen: 24 streams across five homes; no passing profile. Six fully resolved streams lose net dollars under both delays. Other paths remain conditional; no account benefit shown.
about: Five-minute SPY mean reversion as execution timing for a slower ATR breakout.
findings: Authors report about 200 bp CAGR and Sharpe 0.86 in body / 0.87 in abstract to 0.99, including commissions but zero slippage. Our frozen futures design has no passing profile.
mechanism: A short-lived reversal may improve slower-signal execution, but missed momentum and deferred-stop loss can outweigh savings.
build_on: Preserve execution reference and completed negative study. No new waiting-window variant, promotion or account stage earned.
code_feasibility: Committed causal Python fixed-virtual-parent wrapper exists; native parent regeneration, MultiCharts parity and independent verification are not established.
source_revision: Carlo Zarattini and Alberto Pagani, Concretum QuanTips #2, February 2026, seven-page owned upload.
trial_scope: Separate explicit direct-user cross-book project user-fast-alpha-books-20261108, following N15 precedent; not a new autonomous scout hypothesis and not charged/reset there.
